questions.prompt: Why is reading ControlSet001 by default a real forensic error?
options: CurrentControlSet is a runtime pointer, and SYSTEM\Select\Current records which set was actually live -- assuming 001 can mean reading a configuration that was not in effect
questions.explanation: It is frequently correct and occasionally not. When wrong, the service configuration, ShimCache, and LSA settings read all belong to an inactive configuration.

questions.prompt: Why must .LOG1 and .LOG2 files be collected alongside a hive?
options: They contain the decryption key for the hive
They hold changes not yet flushed into the hive, which is frequently the newest and most investigation-relevant data
They are required for the hive to be readable
They contain deleted key backups only
questions.explanation: A hive copied from a running system is dirty, and the most recent changes exist only in the transaction logs until replayed.

questions.prompt: Which registry elements carry a LastWriteTime?
options: Keys only -- values do not have their own timestamps
Neither; the registry has no timestamps
questions.explanation: A key's LastWriteTime reflects the last time any value under it changed, which is what allows dating a modification within an otherwise-static key.

questions.prompt: Why are deleted registry keys often still recoverable?
options: Windows keeps a backup hive automatically
Deletion marks the space unallocated rather than overwriting it, so keys frequently remain in hive slack until reused
Deleted keys are moved to a recycle bin hive
They are not recoverable under any circumstances
questions.explanation: This means persistence an attacker installed and later removed may still be recoverable from the hive's unallocated space.
